title: Piercing Statue Solo #085 (힙컷 · P200 정의형 · 몸통 3조각 · 왼팔 투명(자수정) · 오른팔 목재(wenge) · 몸통 [세로 3등분] 석재(lapis lazuli) / 목재(purpleheart) / 내용물(자수정+수정 조각) · 왼허벅지 수조(내용물 물) · 오른허벅지 내용물(시트린+수정 조각) · 체형 still-visible cinched waist beneath · 하이퍼프 · 파스텔피치 · 메이크업 CarnivalGlam · 금속 혼합 · 쥬얼리 반지·팔찌·헤어 장식·목걸이 JQ5)
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut statue multi-material portrait: real face and neck, and a sculpted body made of different materials — her left arm clear crystal, her right arm carved wood, her torso split into three pieces (carved stone, carved wood and solid glass holding embedded objects), her left thigh a glass vessel full of water and her right thigh solid glass holding embedded objects. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips a short way down her thighs, just below the hip line, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her thighs, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Brazilian woman — sun-bronzed glowing skin, gold and copper shimmer eyes, a glossy nude-coral lip, soft pastel-peach hair styled in natural curls gathered into a high rounded puff. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. Her neck, the hollows above her collarbones and the tops of her shoulders carry the same real living skin as her face: visible pores and fine skin grain, a soft sheen of natural skin oils on the highest planes, faint fine peach-fuzz hairs catching the rim light, gentle tonal variation with a natural warm flush, and the fine natural creases of a real neck — never airbrushed, never smooth like plastic. Like any real person she is slightly asymmetrical: a few small natural beauty marks and freckles scattered unevenly, one side of her neck and shoulder very slightly warmer and more freckled than the other.

Piercings: An extreme, overwhelming armour of about two hundred real mixed-metal piercings with a few red-enamel beads among them covering the face, neck and shoulders: a thick mixed-metal septum ring with a smaller ring above it, three mixed-metal rings through each nostril and a small stud at the tip of the nose; two straight mixed-metal bars across the bridge of the nose between the brows; six thick mixed-metal bars stacked through the outer half of each eyebrow; three rows of five small mixed-metal studs across the forehead above the brows; six small studs up each temple on the bone, well clear of the eyes; two rows of six small studs along each cheekbone; a mixed-metal Medusa stud above the lips with a small stud on each side of it; a big mixed-metal hoop, four smaller rings and a snake-bite ring on each side through the lower lip's edge, and six small hoops along the upper lip's edge; a mixed-metal labret stud and five rings through the chin; six small studs along each jaw; a column of five small studs down each side of the neck; on each ear a full dense row of twelve oversized hoops, thick bars, stretched plugs, helix rings and studs from lobe to top, the biggest hoops hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulders; a row of six small mixed-metal studs along each collarbone and a small mixed-metal stud on each shoulder; and twelve fine mixed-metal chains looping from the ear hoops to the nostril rings and the septum ring. The piercings are packed so densely that the rows touch and overlap, leaving only hairline gaps of bare skin between them, until the face reads as a single armour of metal; the eyes and eyelids stay clear. All jewelry is real mixed metal (yellow gold, silver, copper and rose gold, alternating piece by piece), sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Jewelry: besides the piercings she wears well over ten pieces, an extreme maximalist stack of mixed-metal rings on her fingers; well over ten pieces, an extreme maximalist stack of mixed-metal bracelets and bangles on both wrists; well over ten pieces, an extreme maximalist stack of mixed-metal hair ornaments set in her hair; well over ten pieces, an extreme maximalist stack of mixed-metal necklaces and chains resting on her neck, collarbones and upper chest, all of it real, sitting on and over the material of her body and her real neck and hair without covering her eyes, her face or her piercings.

Physique: A still-visible cinched waist beneath a full soft chest, wide curving hips, both thighs clearly separate and individually shaped, her left arm clear crystal, her right arm carved wood, her torso split into three pieces (carved stone, carved wood and solid glass holding embedded objects), her left thigh a glass vessel full of water and her right thigh solid glass holding embedded objects.

Boundary (skin to material, at underarm height): A single straight, horizontal line runs across her body at underarm height, level with both armpits. Real skin above this line — her face, neck, both shoulders, and the very tops of both upper arms. Below this line, completely different materials meet at her body's natural joints (both shoulders, both hips) and at the seams inside the torso, each keeping its own distinct appearance right up to where it touches its neighbour, never blending into it. At the underarm line itself, the material immediately below rises in a small raised step above her skin, casting a crisp shadow. Shards interlock along this line only.

Left arm (shoulder to hand): solid transparent material, solid amethyst crystal, with internal facets and colour zoning, deep violet where thickest and pale lilac at every thin edge, one continuous carved mass, never hollow, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same material. Light passes straight through it; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it.

Right arm (shoulder to hand): carved from ONE solid block of dark wenge wood, a deep near-black wood finely striped with narrow gold-tan pinstripes running through it, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same wood, the grain running unbroken through it. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface.

Torso (underarm line down to where the thighs begin): The torso, from the underarm line down to where the thighs begin, is divided into 3 side-by-side pieces by 2 straight vertical seams, about 29% and 71% of the way across it from the left of the picture to the right. Torso piece 1 (the piece on the left of the picture, left of the first seam): carved from ONE solid block of deep lapis lazuli, a rich royal-blue stone scattered with small glittering flecks of golden pyrite throughout, polished to a hard, cool sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface. Torso piece 2 (the middle piece, between the two seams): carved from ONE solid block of deep violet purpleheart wood, a dense hardwood of rich purple with fine straight grain, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, the grain running unbroken through it. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface. Torso piece 3 (the piece on the right of the picture, right of the second seam): carved from ONE solid block of amethyst crystal, with internal facets and colour zoning, deep violet where thickest and pale lilac at every thin edge, never hollow, never split; suspended deep within it, visible through it like objects frozen inside a single flawless crystal, are dozens of small, jagged clear quartz shards like frozen lightning bolts, each one a brighter, sharper facet than the glass around it, each one fully embedded in the solid material with no cavity and no liquid around it. Light passes through the solid material; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it.

Left thigh (hip down to its tip, a short way down her thighs, just below the hip line): a sculpted vessel of the same clear glass (unmistakably glass: thick, crystal-clear and polished, bright specular reflections, sharp white highlights, tiny trapped bubbles), completely filled to the brim with clear water holding a scattered handful of pale pink cherry-blossom petals drifting slowly inside it, never crowding, mostly open clear water around each one. It curves inward and seals shut into its own smooth, rounded, closed tip, the water continuing unbroken down to that tip. Light passes through; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it.

Right thigh (hip down to its tip, a short way down her thighs, just below the hip line): carved from ONE solid block of golden-yellow citrine crystal, with faint feathery inclusions and colour zoning, deep honey-gold where thickest and pale lemon at every thin edge, never hollow, never split; suspended deep within it, visible through it like objects frozen inside a single flawless crystal, are dozens of small, jagged clear quartz shards like frozen lightning bolts, each one a brighter, sharper facet than the glass around it, each one fully embedded in the solid material with no cavity and no liquid around it. Light passes through the solid material; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it. The right thigh ends in its own smooth, deeply polished rounded tip, finished the way a carved sculpture is finished.

Where each material meets its neighbour (left shoulder, right shoulder, left hip, right hip, and every seam inside the torso), the two distinct materials sit flush against each other with a thin, clean seam, deliberate and precise, never jagged, torn or blended — always the finish of a sculpture, each material keeping its own colour, clarity and surface completely separate from the one beside it. Both thighs stay clearly separate all the way down, never merging into a single base, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a warm rose pink on one side and a soft cream on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle — glowing evenly, marked with a few thin dark vertical lines so the bending of those lines is visible wherever the body is transparent, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, body angled 45 degrees, her left hand resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so a warm rose pink light glances off the left half and a soft cream light glances off the right half — passing straight through the transparent parts (left arm, left thigh, right thigh, torso piece 3), while only reflecting off the opaque parts (right arm, torso piece 1, torso piece 2). A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears. Shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
